VLCC
The situation in the Strait of Hormuz is becoming more precarious by the hour as the US-Iran conflict has intensified again. Several tankers have been hit, and reports suggest that a fully laden VLCC has been abandoned by its crew. The possibility of a major oil spill would of course be a natural disaster but will also bring more focus on the condition of ships which do make it through and their safety when it comes to performing ship to ship operations.

children.title: Suezmax
children.summary: Despite Suezmaxes regaining competitiveness against VLCCs following last week's sharp correction, a front-heavy tonnage list and muted activity have continued to weigh on the rates in West Africa. Meanwhile, Aframaxes remain firmly in the driving seat across the Atlantic.

children.title: Aframax
children.summary: North Sea After a long weekend activity has been slow on the pick up. Natural dates 8-10 window but with a number of relets around and stems a little thin charterers are able to take their time.

children.title: Capesize
children.summary:
Capesize is heating up across all segments, with both C3 and C5 trade routes posting some of the highest numbers seen this year. Last done on C3 Brazil/China today was seen at USD 40.9, setting a new benchmark which hasn't been seen since the peak of
2021.

children.title: Panamax
children.summary: The Panamax market has firmed steadily through the week, with the gains broadening across both basins as the index pushed higher over successive sessions. In the Atlantic the tone is constructive: transatlantic business remains well bid on the back of a replenished cargo book and a tightening nearby tonnage list, while fronthaul has been slower to follow, with owners holding above charterers' ideas on US Gulf and South American grain.

children.title: Supramax
children.summary: The Supramax market remained mixed and largely directionless, with activity picking up selectively across both the Atlantic and Asia. The Atlantic saw pockets of strength, particularly around the USG and South Atlantic, supported by steady demand for grains, petcoke and minor bulks, while Asia remained active but positional with varied tonnage availability between areas.
